title: AI agent firm Instinct raises $1 billion in latest funding round
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

AI agent startup Instinct said Monday it raised $1 billion in a Series C funding round, valuing the company at $10 billion. Sequoia Capital, Benchmark Capital and Coatue participated. The valuation is four times the $2.5 billion figure attached to Instinct’s previous $250 million raise, reported just last month.

Founded in 2025 by Noah Shinn, Instinct is developing a personal assistant designed to carry out everyday tasks. Users can contact it by text or phone and ask it to plan trips, buy groceries, book tickets or cancel subscriptions. Its newer concierge feature can call businesses to arrange appointments and reservations.

The rapid funding reflects investor interest in AI agents that take actions on a user’s behalf rather than simply answer questions. Instinct’s invite-only service has attracted attention for handling practical errands, but the company has not disclosed user totals or growth figures. That leaves outsiders with limited information for judging how its valuation relates to adoption or revenue.

Instinct is entering a more crowded market. Meta’s Muse offers similar assistance and can connect with the company’s social platforms. For Instinct, the challenge is to turn early enthusiasm into a service people rely on regularly while competing with companies that already reach millions of potential users.

Trust may prove just as important as convenience. Completing purchases, managing schedules and handling messages can require access to sensitive personal information. Instinct says it is improving privacy safeguards and systems intended to detect errors in its agents’ responses. Whether those measures satisfy users will matter as the company expands access to its product.

Shinn said the new capital would help bring Instinct to more people and support further development of its personal AI assistant. The round gives the young company substantial resources, but its long-term success will depend on delivering reliable help beyond its early group of users.
